data.name: Nike
data.gender_notes: Nike is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek goddess Nike, meaning 'victory'. In Greek mythology, Nike is the goddess of victory, often depicted as a winged woman. The name Nike carries the meaning “Victory” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Nike usually hope their child will grow to embody victory and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes triumph over challenges and perseverance.
data.etymology: Nike belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victory.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nike total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The Christian name "Nike" is not commonly used due to the association with the Greek goddess of victory. However, in Christianity, victory is often associated with being a follower of God. The name "Nike" can symbolize the victory that comes from having faith and trust in God, and striving to live a virtuous and godly life.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name "Nike" holds a spiritual meaning as a reminder of the ultimate victory that comes from God. It is a call to remember that no matter what trials or challenges we face in life, we can find strength and victory through our faith and reliance on God. The name Nike also serves as a reminder of the spiritual battle that we face daily and the importance of staying focused on our faith and on God's will for our lives.
